$comment: CANONICAL SUGGESTION CATALOGUE — the single source of truth for what this
product offers a user as a starting point, and for the alternatives it offers
after it fails to find something.
ADMISSION RULE: an entry belongs here only when a source that can answer it is
known to exist and to be reachable by the stated roles at the stated trust
level. A chip is a promise; an unanswerable chip spends a user's first click on
a refusal. 'Probably in the handbook' is not sufficient — verify with
`pnpm eval:retrieval --label` and record the evidence in `why`.
TWO GATES, BOTH REAL. `roles` here mirrors the record-level `roles` metadata on
the backing document, NOT just the namespace grant in retrieval-gate.ts. Those
differ: an HOD is granted the `admissions` NAMESPACE, but every record in it is
tagged prospective/student/parent/staff, so an HOD retrieves nothing from it.
Encoding only the namespace grant would ship chips that fail for HODs alone.
`minTrust` is the trust level at which the backing namespace opens (see
TRUST_NAMESPACES). Chips are filtered by the caller's ACTUAL trust, so an
unverified student is never shown a chip whose source their ceiling forbids.
This file is read by episteme-chat (UI) and by episteme-core's retrieval eval
(regression guard). The packages share no workspace, so JSON on disk is the
only representation both can consume without a build step that could drift.

suggestions.label: What can you do?
suggestions.prompt: What can this assistant do and how do I get better answers?
suggestions.why: help/getting-started.md carries both 'What it can answer' and 'Getting better answers'. The platform-help namespace is resolved on its own axis and is visible to every role with no operator bit — see resolvePlatformNamespaces. Labelled as platform-getting-started in the retrieval golden set.

suggestions.label: Exam rules
suggestions.prompt: What are the examination rules and regulations?
suggestions.why: Verified by --label run 2026-08-06 at maxScore 0.794 — the strongest score in the corpus. STUDENTHANDBOOK.pdf in `general` opens at trust 1, so an unverified student reaches it. Labelled as kb-exam-regulations in the golden set. NOTE on `hod`: the general-namespace records list hod, and expandAudienceRoles lets an HOD read student-tagged content, but the probe ran as `student` — the eval's per-role check is what confirms it, and this is the only role claim in the catalogue not yet confirmed by execution.

suggestions.label: Code of conduct
suggestions.prompt: What is the student code of conduct?
suggestions.why: Verified by --label run 2026-08-06 at maxScore 0.776. Labelled as kb-student-conduct in the golden set. Offered to parents deliberately: it replaces the removed 'academic progress' and 'fee payment' chips with the one thing a parent can genuinely be told, and `general` includes the parent audience. Same unconfirmed-by-execution caveat on `hod` as kb-exam-regulations.

suggestions.label: Entry requirements
suggestions.why: admission_policy.html is the sole document in the admissions namespace (51 vectors, corpus probe 2026-08-02), and admissions opens at trust 1. Labelled as kb-admission-requirements in the golden set. `hod` is excluded deliberately: the records are tagged prospective/student/parent/staff, so an HOD retrieves nothing here despite holding the namespace grant.

suggestions.label: Hostel accommodation
suggestions.prompt: How do I apply for hostel accommodation?
suggestions.why: Verified by --label run 2026-08-02 at maxScore 0.797 — the strongest score any candidate produced, and the only ordinary student question the corpus answers end to end. Backed by STUDENTHANDBOOK.pdf in `general`, which opens at trust 1, so an unverified student reaches it. Scoped to the audiences the question is actually for: staff and hod can retrieve it too, but 'how do I apply for a hostel' is not their question. Labelled as kb-hostel-accommodation in the golden set.

suggestions.label: Student services
suggestions.prompt: What student support services are available?
suggestions.why: Verified by --label run 2026-08-06 at maxScore 0.725. Labelled as kb-student-services in the golden set. Placed after the higher-scoring handbook chips so it fills a slot only when a role has one spare; the grid shows four.

suggestions.label: Using the library
suggestions.prompt: How do I use the university library?
suggestions.why: Verified by --label run 2026-08-06 at maxScore 0.770. Labelled as kb-library in the golden set. Student-only: library access is not a question the other audiences ask first.

suggestions.label: Add a document
suggestions.prompt: How do I add a document to the knowledge base?
suggestions.expectedSource: Adding documents to the knowledge base
suggestions.why: Directly the subject of admin/ingesting-documents.md. Labelled as platform-ingest-howto. The operator bit is mandatory — platform-admin-hidden-from-non-operator asserts this exact query must abstain without it, so showing the chip to a non-operator would guarantee a refusal.

suggestions.label: Onboard staff
suggestions.prompt: How do I onboard new staff and set their access levels?
suggestions.expectedSource: Onboarding users and setting access levels
suggestions.why: Labelled as platform-onboarding-access. This is the Rule 1d case: a PLATFORM question about creating accounts and assigning roles, not a university HR policy question — which is why it resolves even though no institutional HR document exists.

suggestions.label: Institution setup
suggestions.prompt: How do I set up my institution in Episteme?
suggestions.why: Directly the subject of admin/institution-setup.md. Labelled as platform-institution-setup.

candidates.prompt: What medical and health services are available?
candidates.blockedOn: Retrieves (0.749) and is shippable — held back only because the grid shows four chips and the higher-scoring handbook entries already fill a student's row. Promote if one of those is retired.

candidates.prompt: What happens if a student breaks the rules?
candidates.blockedOn: Retrieves (0.699), but overlaps kb-student-conduct almost entirely. Two chips onto the same handbook section spends a scarce slot twice.

candidates.prompt: Which office do I contact about student records?
candidates.blockedOn: Retrieves (0.734). Deliberately NOT a chip: its value is as the abstention path's grounded escalation — the redirect offered when a records question finds nothing. Promoting it to the welcome grid would invite it as an opening question, which is not what it is for. Guarded as kb-records-office in the golden set.

candidates.prompt: What are the key postgraduate dates for the 2026 session?
candidates.blockedOn: Retrieves (0.767) but is doubly narrow: trust 3+ AND postgraduate-only. The catalogue cannot express 'postgraduate' as a filter, so shipping it would show a PG-only chip to every verified undergraduate. Needs a programme/level dimension first.

$rejected: Transcript, course registration, registration deadlines, CGPA and fees were probed on 2026-08-02 and retrieved NOTHING. They are not pending — they are unsupported until a document is ingested. Moved to `unsupported` below.

'Who is the vice chancellor' DOES retrieve (0.694) but is deliberately excluded: the only source is STUDENTHANDBOOK.pdf dated 2022-12-19, so the answer would be a confidently-cited, possibly-former post-holder. Post-holder questions belong to the news/web tier.

$comment: Removed from the shipped set with the reason, so nobody re-adds them from
intuition. Each was a chip in the previous hardcoded list.
These are not 'not written yet' — they are unanswerable given the current
corpus, and adding a document is what changes that, not editing this file.

entries.was: Give me a study plan and tips for upcoming exams
entries.reason: Out of domain by Rule 3 — generic tutoring, not institutional information. The agent is required to decline it.

entries.was: Scholarships and funding / fee payment / outstanding fees
entries.reason: The financial-aid namespace holds zero records, and trust 1-2 cannot reach it even if it did.
No grades data in the corpus and no tool exposes it. Implies a capability the product does not have.

entries.was: Department overview, staff management, accreditation, budget (all HOD chips)
entries.reason: staff-internal holds zero records, and the admissions/academic-policy records exclude the hod role. An HOD can currently retrieve only the student handbook.

entries.was: Claim review workflow, department reporting, compliance report
entries.reason: No platform doc and no institutional document covers these.
The programmes namespace holds zero records. Entry requirements are covered by admission_policy instead — see kb-admission-requirements.
Probed 2026-08-02 (kb-todo-transcript): retrieved nothing. No records procedure is ingested.

entries.was: Exam preparation / how is CGPA calculated
entries.reason: Probed 2026-08-02 (kb-todo-cgpa): retrieved nothing. `academic-policy` holds a postgraduate CALENDAR, not grading policy.
Retrieves (0.694) but only from STUDENTHANDBOOK.pdf dated 2022-12-19 — it would name a possibly-former post-holder with full confidence. A chip must not point at a known staleness trap.
